storyboard.ears: Americans quietly abandoned the home phone, and scammers moved into the silence.
By 2024, 76 percent of US adults had no landline, triple the share in 2010. The old home phone is nearly extinct.
storyboard.eyes: substance: the phone wires; cause: Data saws through each home's phone line at the pole and the line drops
storyboard.evidence: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), CDC | Share of US adults with no landline (wireless-only) | https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nhis/earlyrelease/wireless202506.pdf | 2026-08-21

storyboard.ears: Scams were 22 percent of 2024 robocalls, and telemarketing was even bigger. So most calls are trying to sell or trick you.
storyboard.eyes: substance: the board's call lamps; cause: Data plugs each cord into its jack by hand and that kind of call lights up across the board
storyboard.evidence: YouMail | US robocalls in 2024, by category | https://blog.youmail.com/2025/02/what-the-2024-robocall-review-tells-us-about-spam-calls/ | 2026-08-21

storyboard.ears: Americans got 52.8 billion robocalls in 2024, nearly double 2016. As landlines vanished, unwanted calls only multiplied, so unknown numbers now feel risky.
storyboard.evidence: YouMail | Total US robocalls per year, 2016 vs. 2024 | https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/us-consumers-received-nearly-4-4-billion-robocalls-in-december-52-8-billion-in-all-of-2024--according-to-youmail-robocall-index-302348867.html | 2026-08-21

storyboard.ears: Your phone still rings, but most robocalls want your money, not you.
